summary: Implemented PostgreSQL-aware SQL statement splitting and integrated whole-file validation into the migration runner while preserving the public API, discovery behavior, ledger schema, patch seam, console summaries, and per-file commits.
implementation: Preserves original statement text with outer whitespace stripped; discards empty and comment-only fragments.
Handles ordinary and E/e strings, doubled quotes, quoted identifiers, case-sensitive ASCII dollar delimiters, identifier-embedded dollar text, CR/LF line comments, and nested block comments.
Rejects unterminated quoted regions and block comments before executing any statement from that file.
Uses the existing psycopg connection context for rollback on failure; earlier file commits remain durable.
coverage: Added lexical edge cases, adjacent quoted tokens, full-file validation, UTF-8, immediate SQL-file discovery, empty-file recording, and real PostgreSQL tests for function/DO bodies, nested comments, rerun skipping, per-file rollback, and durable earlier migrations.
limitations: This is a statement-boundary lexer, not SQL grammar validation.
COPY FROM STDIN data, transaction-control statements, psql commands, non-ASCII dollar tags, concurrent migration coordination, and checksum tracking remain outside the task scope.
